newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on crude, IPE.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on crude, IPE.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps firmed midday Friday on higher overnight crude and gas oil futures in the West with Asian fundamentals remaining bearish, traders said.
"The market rose this morning because of the IPE. Fundamentally it is still bearish as there are a lot of prompt supplies around," one trader said.
Gas oil swaps were last quoted at $26.15/$25.35 per barrel up from Thursday's $25.85/$25.95, brokers said. The market traded earlier at $25.25 per barrel.
February Brent crude closed up 41 cents to $23.18 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) while February gas oil was up $7.50 per tonne to $212.00 on Thursday.
Traders said the Singapore market is still bogged down by surplus prompt cargoes with sellers forced to offload product on a floating basis at below Singapore spot quotes on a free-on-board basis.

The front month regrade or jet fuel/gas oil spread widened further due to the strong buying interest for prompt physical jet fuel cargoes which has stretched the physical spread between the two products.
The February regrade was last quoted notionally at $4.00/$4.50 per barrel from Thursday's $3.80/$4.00, brokers said.
On Thursday, 150,000 barrels of physical jet fuel traded at $30.75 per barrel while gas oil was offered to a low of $25.40 per barrel, both on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
Fuel oil swaps rose notionally in line with the firmer crude with February last quoted at $100.50/$101.50 per tonne, up 50 cents from Thursday.

Naphtha rose with the crude hike with February quoted at $24.20/$24.60 per barrel from Thursday's $24.10/$24.30 per barrel, one broker said. Brokers said buyers were hesitant because they felt the recent crude rally may run out of steam shortly.
